commits.message: A focused Dropdown's filter is the terminal's own cursor: where the painter shows it, the caret is a blank cell marked caretMark("bar"), its side set by ordering; labeled takes its label as segments so the mark survives ordering (rich-control-codes-xh4n.okr)

A bar caret in a right-to-left run stands on the insertion point's edge: Style.caret is a CaretMark, its shape and the side of its cell the insertion point is on, read off the levels the row is ordered by (rich-control-codes-xh4n.e1h) (#565)

* A bar caret in a right-to-left run stands on the insertion point's edge: Style.caret is a CaretMark, its shape and the side of its cell the insertion point is on, read off the levels the row is ordered by (rich-control-codes-xh4n.e1h)

* The caret's side is set where the row is ordered: orient's displayed turns a caret mark to the level its glyph is shown at, so a masked or pictured row puts the bar where its shown glyphs do; CaretMark is branded to caretMark (rich-control-codes-xh4n.e1h)

BREAKING: Style.withCaret and StyleOptions.caret take a CaretMark (caretMark(shape, side)), not a CaretShape.

Review (high): caretSide re-derived levels from the raw value; replaced. Search bar keeps measure. The paint clamp for a right-side bar in the last column stays: no column exists past the screen's edge.

* caretMark takes a shape only: a mark stands on its glyph's leading edge and ordering alone sets a right side (caretMarkOn), so no caller states an edge for orient to contradict; one turned style per row (rich-control-codes-xh4n.e1h)

* Only a bar caret turns; the docs promise the leading edge, not where a typed character lands; paint steps one grapheme (rich-control-codes-xh4n.e1h)
